title: Second Benchmark Project Selection — LedgerFlow Lite

selectedProject.name: LedgerFlow Lite
selectedProject.description: A small invoicing/expense system with approval workflow, line items, financial calculations, and reporting.
selectedProject.complexity: 14-16 FRs — moderately higher than TeamFlow Lite (11 FRs)

whyDifferentFromTeamFlowLite: TeamFlow Lite was task/workflow management. LedgerFlow Lite is financial operations.
New domain: financial calculations (tax, totals), line items, approval chains, reporting/aggregation.
Different data model: customers/vendors instead of teams/members, invoices instead of tasks, line items instead of comments.
New competency requirements: CSV export, dashboard aggregation, amount validation.
whatNewSimplificationRisksItExposes: Financial calculation correctness — simple implementation may produce wrong totals/tax.
Line item relationships — 1:N relationship with cascade that differs from task→comment.
Approval workflow with permission checks — more nuanced than task status transitions.
Dashboard/reporting — aggregation queries that test whether v0.4 Manual Router catches complexity.
CSV export — testing whether v0.4 produces deterministic, verifiable output.
whyComplexEnoughButNotTooLarge: 14-16 FRs is moderate — above TeamFlow Lite's 11 but far below enterprise ERP (50+ FRs).
Financial domain adds real-world validation complexity without requiring payment gateways.
Line items + approval + dashboard are distinct enough to test multi-entity relationships.
Can be built as a monolith (anti-overengineering rule) — no microservices needed.
Estimated implementation: 500-800 lines of backend + 400-600 lines of frontend.
whyV04FactoryLiteShouldHelp: Manual Router should classify LedgerFlow Lite as a business-tool/SaaS, routing to appropriate starter.
Proof-of-Read ensures requirements for financial calculations are read before implementing.
Contamination logging keeps Vanilla and v0.4 runs independent.
Evidence hierarchy prevents counting CSV stubs or placeholder dashboards as real features.
Anti-gaming controls catch fake financial calculations and placeholder approval workflows.
